new_statements.translation: 2.1.2. Stress is absent in Boko. Four phonological tones are distinguished in Boko: ultra-high (uH), high (H), low (L) and ultra-low (uL): gba̋ 'leg', gbá 'gift', gbà 'door'; pa̋ 'to sting', pá 'to fill', pȁ 'full' (on the tone notation of different authors see 1.4.0). Tones within a word may combine in practically any sequence, cf. ba̋a̋ 'skin', ba̋à 'to ask', báá 'pancreas', báà 'share', báȁ 'even', bȁa̋ 'father', bȁá 'opposite side', bȁȁ 'fourth daughter', etc.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Boko has no word stress; it is a four-level register tone language (ultra-high, high, low, ultra-low) in which tone is lexical and grammatical and tones combine freely within the word. The sketch also states (2.2.1, p. 1054) that there is no need to posit a foot, and that intonation has limited functions.
new_statements.exceptions: None. Contextual tone changes are described (ultra-high lowers to high next to non-uH syllables; uH of the first element of an attributive NP lowers to low; an NP cannot end in ultra-low; perfective marked by ultra-low tone).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement in the standard Jazyki mira 2.1.2 'suprasegmentals' slot; tone examples are citation forms. Chapter is a compilation from published materials (preface p. 13: primarily Jones 1998/2004, partly Prost and Wedekind), not fieldwork. The whole volume is openly hosted by the Institute of Linguistics RAS.
new_statements.identity_note: The chapter describes Boko proper (boko1266, ISO bqc), covering both the Benin and Nigeria varieties (sec. 2.7.0 notes Benin dialects lose intervocalic consonants); it treats Busa (busa1253, bqp) and Bokobaru (boko1267, bus) as separate closest languages and cites Bokobaru forms only as comparanda. The source is a compiled sketch (Perekhvalskaya did no fieldwork; based on Jones 1998/2004, Prost 1976/1981, Wedekind), so the statement is second-order relative to Jones 1998, which was not opened.

(stress is absent in Boko); four phonological level tones (ultra-high, high, low, ultra-low) combining freely within the word; p. 1054: contextual tone lowering, NP cannot end in ultra-low, perfective by tone change, intonation limited, nasalization syllable-prosodic; sec. 2.2.1: no need to posit a foot. Chapter compiled from Jones 1998/2004, Prost 1976/1981, Funke 1915 (preface p. 13: 'primarily R. Jones, partly A. Prost and K. Wedekind').
